title: Model predicts sudden late remodelling of apparently stable biological patterns

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Model predicts sudden late remodelling of apparently stable biological patterns

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the neural cellular automaton suddenly remodelled cell fates after a long period of quiescent, stable pattern, the authors predict that something similar may occur in biological systems: some phenotypes that appear complete may need to be followed much longer to see their true dynamics.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Experimental results on repatterning of planaria

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The sudden remodelling of cell fates after a long period of apparently quiescent, stable pattern in our model (figure 4) predicts that something similar may occur in biological systems.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Experimental results on repatterning of planaria”. Scope: Regenerating and developing organisms, tested in planaria

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-13: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.44

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction is measurable once a duration and event definition are chosen, but suitable long-running image series are not known to cover its broad biological scope. A decisive test therefore needs prospective long-term observation rather than re-reading endpoint figures.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify biological patterns declared morphologically stable, follow them with repeated imaging well beyond their usual endpoint, and estimate the incidence and timing of spontaneous fate remodelling. Persistent stability in adequately powered long-duration cohorts would refute the prediction for the tested systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sparse late events are vulnerable to survivorship and husbandry confounds.

Most experiments stop observation when the expected endpoint is reached.

The claim does not specify taxa, frequency, or a minimum quiescent interval.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The planarian version of the prediction is measurable, but the only quantitative series is this paper's own aggregate, and the supplementary file is a document of figures rather than a reusable cohort table. Independent long-term imaging after a scored stable phenotype is not in a public dataset. Re-reading the paper's figure is not a test of the prediction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Follow individual regenerating or developing animals after an apparently stable phenotype and record whether anatomy changes again without a new intervention, using the planarian cutoff of any morphology change after four weeks. Repeated independent cohorts in which a non-trivial fraction remodel after long stability would support the prediction; large cohorts followed well past that window with no late change would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Late change can be produced by starvation, infection, or residual drug rather than an intrinsic return to an anatomical trajectory.

No public animal-level longitudinal morphology table covers the weeks after apparent regenerative completion.

The wording is that something similar may occur, so failure to see late remodelling does not refute it.
